content:
Decimals to thousandths, point-shifting by 10/100/1000 and decimal arithmetic — precision marks on every Class 5 Olympiad paper. Here is what the IMO Class 5 decimals chapter tests, with a free 10-question test.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Decimals chapter tests

  • Place value to thousandths
  • Multiplying and dividing by 10, 100, 1000
  • All four operations on decimals
  • Fraction ↔ decimal conversions and rounding

Key facts your child should know

  • × 10/100/1000 moves the point right; ÷ moves it left.
  • 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500 — padding zeros changes nothing.
  • Count decimal places when multiplying: 0.3 × 0.7 = 0.21.
  • 1/8 = 0.125; 3/4 = 0.75; 1/5 = 0.2.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Moving the point the wrong way.
  • Misaligning points in addition.
  • Dropping the zero in answers like 0.07.

quiz.title: IMO Class 5 Decimals Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Write each with 3 decimal places, then sort smallest to largest: 0.06, 0.6, 0.606, 0.66.
307/1000 means 307 divided by 1000, so it is 0.307.
Line up the decimal points (write 6.05 as 6.050) and subtract: 6.05 − 4.275 = 1.775.

questions.q: Which of these is the expanded form of 9.254?
Express 2.35 as a mixed fraction in lowest terms.
questions.explanation: 2.35 = 2 + 350/1000. Dividing 350/1000 by the HCF 50 gives 7/20, so the answer is 2 7/20.

options: Nine and three hundred four thousandths
Nine and three hundred four hundredths
questions.explanation: 9.304 = 9 + 304/1000, read as nine and three hundred four thousandths.

questions.q: Express 0.6 as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.explanation: 0.6 = 600/1000. Divide the top and bottom by 200 to get 3/5.
Line up the decimal points and add: 0.605 + 0.395 = 1.

questions.q: In the number 9.187, what is the place value of the digit 7?
questions.explanation: The digit 7 sits in the thousandths place, so its place value is 7 thousandths = 0.007.

questions.q: Write 6 ones + 5 hundredths + 8 thousandths as a decimal.
questions.explanation: Put each part in its own place and fill empty places with 0: 6 ones + 5 hundredths + 8 thousandths = 6.058.

faq.q: What happens when you multiply a decimal by 100?
faq.a: The decimal point moves two places to the right: 3.45 × 100 = 345.
Pad to the same length: 0.50 vs 0.45 — so 0.5 is greater.
